title: Chain-of-Thought Is Not Explainability
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31271v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) allows language models to verbalise multi-step rationales before producing their final answer. While this technique often boosts task performance and offers an impression of transparency into the model's reasoning, this position paper argues that rationales generated by current CoT techniques can be misleading and are neither necessary nor sufficient for trustworthy interpretability. We analyse faithfulness as whether CoTs are not only human-interpretable but also reflect the model's underlying reasoning well enough to support responsible use. By synthesising evidence from prior work, we systematically show that verbalised chains are frequently unfaithful, diverging from the critical hidden computations that drive a model's predictions. As CoT is increasingly relied upon in application domains, including high-stakes ones such as medicine, law, and autonomous systems, we further argue that this unfaithfulness is not taken seriously enough in these settings: our analysis of 1,000 recent CoT-centric papers finds that approximately 21.7% explicitly treat CoT as a load-bearing interpretability technique, building pipelines or safety arguments that would not hold if CoT is unfaithful to the model's actual reasoning. They include papers in high-stakes domains that heavily hinge on such interpretability claims. Building on prior work, we make three proposals: (i) avoid treating CoT as being sufficient for interpretability without additional verification, (ii) adopt rigorous methods that assess faithfulness for downstream decision-making, and (iii) report such assessments alongside any interpretability claims based on CoT, while continuing to use CoT for its communicative and monitoring benefits.
relevance_reason: Key author: Yoshua Bengio

title: Understanding the Importance of Massive Activations through Adversarial Robustness
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32585v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A common occurrence in Large Language Models (LLMs) is the emergence of so-called massive activations. This phenomenon is well known in the literature and has been connected to attention sinks, representational compression, as well as signal propagation. However, the reasons and consequences for their appearance are not yet well understood. In this paper, we explain the role of massive activations in deep learning by showing that they are connected to the region migration phenomenon in delayed robustness. Under the spline theoretic interpretation of deep networks, we show that massive activations push the representations away from the nonlinearity boundaries of the network, decreasing the complexity of its input-output map around data points. Furthermore, we uncover for the first time that this phenomenon is not unique to transformers and actually appears in a number of common architectures performing simple supervised learning tasks. We validate this connection through extensive experiments on a diverse set of architectures including residual MLP, ResNet18, Vision Transformers and GPT and datasets including MNIST, CIFAR10, Imagenette and Shakespeare Text. We consistently observe that massive activations and region migration co-occur with adversarial robustness. Furthermore, we illustrate that this connection holds in the large-scale pretraining of LLMs by showing that the rise of massive activations in LLMs closely tracks the adversarial accuracy of the model under perturbations of the token embeddings.
relevance_reason: Key author: Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato

title: AVQ-Attention-2: Adaptive Vector-Quantized Attention with Exact Local Blocks and Linear-Cost Training
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32989v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attention costs $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ in the number of tokens. Vector-quantized attention reduces this to $\mathcal{O}(NM)$ by clustering the $N$ keys, attending to the $M$ codewords instead, and its adaptive form, AVQ-attention, concentrates codebook resolution where a query's attention mass actually falls. We present AVQ-Attention-2, a better design that merges it with exact local attention and attends to the mean of each cluster's keys rather than to a codeword. We show three improvements: consistently better quality at comparable cost; training that now also costs $\mathcal{O}(NM)$ rather than $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$; and an approximation accurate enough that the layer can be dropped into a pretrained transformer without fine-tuning. Across a variety of sequence lengths the result is competitive not merely with other approximate attention but with exact dense attention, running faster than FlashAttention at little to no loss in quality.
relevance_reason: Key author: Max Welling

title: ProFL: Performative Robust Optimal Federated Learning
abstract:
arXiv:2410.18075v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Performative prediction is a framework that captures distribution shifts that occur during the training of machine learning models due to their deployment. As the trained model is used, the induced data distribution evolves, leading to deviations from the original data distribution. The impact of such model-induced distribution shifts in federated learning (FL) is increasingly likely to transpire in real-life use cases. A recently proposed approach extends performative prediction to FL with the resulting model converging to a performative stable point, which may be far from the performative optimal point. Earlier research in centralized settings has shown that the performative optimal point can be achieved under model-induced distribution shifts, but these approaches require the performative risk to be convex and the training data to be noiseless. These assumptions are often violated in realistic FL systems. This paper addresses these limitations and proposes Performative Robust Optimal Federated Learning (ProFL), an algorithm that targets the performative optimal point in FL while mitigating the effects of noisy and contaminated local data. We present a neighborhood-convergence analysis under the Polyak--Lojasiewicz condition, which applies to non-convex objectives. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the advantage of Robust Optimal Federated Learning over the state-of-the-art.
relevance_reason: Key author: Tian Xie

title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32761v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Heat flow across the core-mantle boundary (CMB) depends on the lattice thermal conductivity ($\kappa_{\mathrm{latt}}$) of lowermost-mantle minerals, yet calculated CMB values for MgO differ severalfold, and high-temperature estimates of the conductivity increase across the bridgmanite-post-perovskite transition range from about 20 to 50%. Direct solutions of the linearized phonon Boltzmann transport equation (LBTE) require thousands of density functional theory (DFT) force evaluations per thermodynamic state. Here we replace these evaluations with phase-specific, fine-tuned MACE potentials for MgO, MgSiO3 bridgmanite (Pv), and MgSiO3 post-perovskite (PPv). The potentials reproduce DFT energies, forces, stresses, pressure-volume relations, and compressed-state phonons for all three phases. For MgO at 0 GPa, replacing MACE forces with DFT forces in otherwise identical transport calculations changes $\kappa_{\mathrm{latt}}$ by 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K. PPv is 44-55% more conductive than Pv at the same pressure and temperature and strongly anisotropic, with $\kappa_{[100]}/\kappa_{[010]}$ ranging from 1.7 to 2.1. The quasi-harmonic phase boundary has a Clapeyron slope of $(7.4 \pm 0.1)$ MPa/K and intersects a model geotherm at 116.2 GPa and 2660 K, where the transition raises the silicate conductivity by 47%, to 8.6 W/(m K). Heating in the basal thermal boundary layer lowers the MgO and PPv conductivities to 37.3 and 6.7 W/(m K) at the CMB, where Hashin-Shtrikman bounds of 9.5-11.4 W/(m K) for an Fe-free aggregate of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO encompass the 10 W/(m K) used in earlier heat-flow estimates. The density-temperature parameterizations provide an intrinsic end-member reference for lower-mantle thermal models.
relevance_reason: Development/fine-tuning and benchmarking of MACE machine-learned interatomic potentials (validated against DFT energies, forces, stresses, phonons) used to drive phonon Boltzmann transport for MgO and MgSiO3 polymorphs; (a)-(c) all clearly satisfied.

title: OMNI-P3x universal neural network potential for large-scale computational photochemistry workflows
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32133v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computational photochemistry supports the design and understanding of new materials. However, the high cost of excited-state quantum-mechanical (QM) calculations makes screening large molecular libraries prohibitively expensive. To address this limitation, we introduce OMNI-P3x, a universal machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) for singlet ground- and excited-state simulations of neutral and charged organic molecules. Trained on both ground- and excited-state conformations, it performs complete computational photochemistry workflows with accuracy approaching TD-DFT. We demonstrate its practical applicability by screening a combinatorial library of 234,375 flavylium derivatives, where the pretrained model performs ground-state geometry optimization and predicts absorption properties without additional QM calculations. Following fine-tuning, we further screen 162,960 xanthene-based dyes, identifying new candidates for red, near-infrared and short-wavelength infrared emission. Furthermore, state-dependent neural charges, learned without reference atomic charges, provide an interpretable picture of intramolecular charge redistribution upon excitation.
relevance_reason: A universal MLIP trained for ground/excited states and applied to geometry optimization and photochemistry screening of explicit atomic molecules satisfies (a)-(c).

title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32851v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit. However, such refinement remains difficult for dynamical observables because differentiating chaotic molecular trajectories yields unstable gradients. Here, we introduce PathGrad, which differentiates Langevin path probabilities instead of the trajectories themselves. The resulting gradient estimator is accumulated on the fly from thermal noise and force derivatives, and its variance remains stable as the trajectory length increases. We validated the gradient estimator against finite-difference calculations and used it to fine-tune molten-copper and water potentials against experimental diffusion coefficients together with structural constraints. For water, jointly optimizing diffusion and the oxygen-oxygen radial distribution function also improves the predictions of shear viscosity and rotational relaxation, neither of which is included in the optimization objective. Alignment at a single temperature also improves the apparent activation energies of multiple dynamical observables, bringing their temperature dependences closer to experiments. Moreover, the optimized potential exhibits smaller force errors relative to an independent, higher-level quantum-chemical reference, indicating that alignment with experiments improves the fidelity of the potential energy surface beyond the fitted targets. PathGrad thus establishes a general framework for incorporating experimental observables directly into force field optimizations.
relevance_reason: PathGrad differentiates Langevin path probabilities to refine ML force fields against dynamical MD observables on explicit atoms, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Neutron Spectroscopy Transformed: Deuterated ZIF-8 and Machine-Learned Potentials Catch Nitrogen Threading Its Gates
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32739v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We report a step change in what inelastic neutron scattering (INS) can reveal, by combining machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with deliberate deuteration of the sample. INS's prowess in charting framework and guest motions within porous materials during in situ dosing has historically had one caveat: costly density-functional-theory calculations are a major bottleneck in the speed and depth of analysis. We show that rapid frontier MLIPs remove this bottleneck on both counts, keeping pace with the experiment while bringing a new level of insight. Deuterating the linkers of ZIF-8 pries apart bands that overlap in the hydrogenous framework, and we test four MLIPs against eight stages of nitrogen dosing at 77 K. On loading, a previously unobserved band appears at 270 cm^-1 and grows gradually through the dosing series. The simulations trace it to single N2 molecules threaded end-on through four-ring windows, each turning its ring of linkers and propping the window open, and unbiased dynamics catch molecules threading into the windows on their own, finding a free-energy trap that crowding stabilizes. This is the first vibrational signature of the threaded state and, crucially, its intensity directly counts the threading over the slow, macroscopic timescale of gas uptake, in situ. More broadly, the simulations explain how each framework band responds to its guests, establishing MLIP-assisted inelastic neutron scattering as a route to mechanism, not just assignment.
relevance_reason: MLIP benchmarking and MLIP-driven MD/free-energy analysis of N2 threading in deuterated ZIF-8 against INS uses explicit atoms and satisfies (a)-(c).

title: Accelerating Equivariant Interatomic Potentials for Molecular Dynamics through Radial tabulation and Kernel Fusion
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31865v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) achieve near-quantum-chemical accuracy, but their computational cost and GPU memory footprint restrict molecular dynamics (MD) at extended length and time scales. Even when the tensor product (TP) is accelerated, both bottlenecks remain governed by evaluating and storing per-edge radial weights in the NequIP convolution. We introduce JET-MLIPs (Joint-Kernel Equivariant Convolution with Tabulated Radial Weights for MLIP simulation), a GPU backend applicable to pretrained NequIP-family potentials without retraining. JET-MLIPs replaces the radial multilayer perceptron (MLP) with a piecewise cubic Hermite table and fuses table lookup, spherical harmonics, TP and neighbor aggregation into a single kernel, eliminating per-edge radial-weight and MLP-intermediate storage during force evaluation. Across 15 released potentials from SevenNet, MACE, NequIP-OAM, Nequix and EquFlash on a 5632-atom liquid electrolyte, LAMMPS MD attains 1.5-5.9$\times$ step-time speed-ups and 2.4-24$\times$ peak memory reductions relative to each family's existing TP-accelerated backend on a single H200 GPU while preserving single-precision (fp32) accuracy and dynamical stability. These reductions enable multi-nanosecond transport-property simulations of roughly $10^4$-atom systems on a single GPU and broaden access to large-scale equivariant MLIP MD on widely available GPUs.
relevance_reason: NequIP-family machine-learned interatomic potential acceleration benchmarked in LAMMPS molecular dynamics on explicit atoms satisfies (a)-(c) as MLIP/MD method development.

title: Comparative Molecular Dynamics Study of Initial Oxide Film Growth on Al, Mg, and Ti Using a Universal Neural Network Potential
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32659v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spontaneous formation of an oxide film, which may be passive, is found in many metals such as Al and Ti. We report direct computational observation of oxide film formation on the three major light structural metals, Al, Mg, and Ti, with molecular dynamics (MD) using a universal neural network potential (NNP). O2 molecules were supplied during MD simulations to replenish O consumed by the metal. Al and Ti formed a 1-2 nm thick film within a few ps of the simulation with O2 gas pressure of 102-103 atm. The film thicknesses of all metal oxides continued to increase proportionally to the logarithm of simulation time, consistent with Cabrera-Mott theory. Al and Ti oxides grow at the surface, while Mg oxide grows into the Mg metal. Al, Mg, and Ti are approximately 4.4, 4.3, and 5.2-fold coordinated, respectively, in the oxide.
relevance_reason: Universal neural-network-potential-driven molecular dynamics of oxide film growth on explicit Al/Mg/Ti surfaces satisfies (a)-(c) as an MLIP-MD application.

title: Anharmonic enhancement of thermal conductivity in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$: A consistent picture from molecular dynamics and Wigner transport
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Anharmonicity limits heat conduction in crystals, but its role in amorphous solids, where heat is carried mainly by tunneling between quasi-degenerate vibrations, remains unsettled. Here we disentangle the contributions of structural disorder, quantum statistics, and anharmonicity to the thermal conductivity of amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ (aGST), the prototypical phase-change memory material. Using a single machine-learned potential trained on first-principles data, we compare classical equilibrium and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (MD), which include anharmonicity to all orders, with harmonic Allen-Feldman theory and the anharmonic Wigner transport equation, both of which include quantum statistics. Four MD approaches agree on a conductivity of 0.171-0.181 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, about 16% above the harmonic Allen-Feldman value for the same model, and the Wigner formulation bridges the two: with classical statistics, it agrees with MD to within 5%. We trace this anharmonic enhancement to vibrational couplings that grow with the frequency difference between modes, so that anharmonic broadening opens additional channels for heat conduction. A comparison with silica, alumina, and disordered carbons reveals three regimes, in which anharmonicity reduces, barely affects, or enhances the conductivity. The predicted glass-like increase of the conductivity with temperature is consistent with thermoreflectance measurements. These results show that anharmonicity has no universal effect in disordered solids, and can promote rather than limit heat transport in strongly disordered materials.
relevance_reason: Machine-learned potential trained on first-principles data driving equilibrium/non-equilibrium MD of amorphous Ge2Sb2Te5 to compute thermal conductivity and compare with Wigner transport; (a) explicit atoms, (b) MLIP plus MD, (c) applied to heat transport, all satisfied.

title: Nanoindentation induced plasticity in equiatomic MoTaW alloys by experimentally guided machine learning molecular dynamics simulations
abstract:
arXiv:2601.06846v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCA) exhibit exceptional strength and thermal stability, yet their plastic deformation mechanisms under complex contact loading remain insufficiently understood. Here, the nanoindentation response of an equiatomic MoTaW alloy is investigated through a combined experimental and atomistically resolved modeling approach. Spherical nanoindentation experiments are coupled with large scale molecular dynamics simulations employing a tabulated low dimensional Gaussian Approximation Potential (tabGAP), enabling near DFT accuracy. A physics based similarity criterion, implemented via PCA of load-displacement curves, is used to identify mechanically representative experimental responses for quantitative comparison with simulations. Indentation stress-strain curves are constructed yielding excellent agreement in the elastic regime between experiment and simulation, with reduced Young's moduli of approximately 270 GPa. Generalized stacking fault energy calculations reveal elevated unstable stacking- and twinning-fault energies in MoTaW relative to pure refractory elements, indicating suppressed localized shear and a preference for dislocation-mediated plasticity. Atomistic analyses demonstrate a strong crystallographic dependence of plastic deformation, with symmetric {110}<111> slip activation and four-fold rosette pile-ups for the [001] orientation, and anisotropic slip, strain localization, and enhanced junction formation for [011]. Local entropy and polyhedral template matching analyses further elucidate dislocation network evolution and deformation-induced local structural transformations. Overall, this study establishes a direct mechanistic link between fault energetics, orientation-dependent dislocation activity, and experimentally observed nanoindentation behavior in RCCA.
relevance_reason: Large-scale MD nanoindentation simulations using a tabulated GAP machine-learned interatomic potential plus stacking-fault energy calculations, clearly satisfying MLIP development/application (a)-(c).

title: In silico  design and prediction of M-sandwiched MCP (M = Cu, Ag, Au) compounds featuring buckled phosphidocarbide sheets
abstract: A new family of ternary MCP phosphidocarbide compounds (M = Cu, Ag, Au) is predicted by combining evolutionary crystal structure prediction with density functional theory calculations. Inspired by an analogy with buckled phosphorene-in which one P atom per formula unit is replaced by C− and charge-compensated by an intercalated M+ cation-the ground-state structures crystallize in the polar trigonal R3m space group for all three compositions. Their viability is supported by the absence of imaginary phonon modes, satisfaction of the Born–Huang elastic stability criteria, and short-time structural persistence up to 1200 K in ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, despite near-zero or positive formation enthalpies relative to the elemental reference states-consistent with dynamically and mechanically robust metastable phases. HSE06 calculations with spin–orbit coupling reveal tunable electronic properties across the series: CuCP and AgCP are indirect-band-gap semiconductors (1.11 and 1.02 eV, respectively), while AuCP is a semimetal. At higher photon energies, all three compounds exhibit strong ultraviolet absorption, with absorption coefficients reaching the order of 106 cm−1. These results establish MCP compounds, built from buckled polyanionic [CP]− layers separated by M+ cations, as a new class of phosphidocarbides with metal-tunable electronic properties and strongly anisotropic mechanical and UV optical responses. Phosphorene substitution thus emerges as a general design route to related phases.
relevance_reason: Evolutionary crystal structure prediction combined with DFT, phonons, and ab initio MD satisfies (a)-(c) by predicting and validating explicit atomistic structures.

title: A deep-learning potential for predicting thermal and physical properties of high-entropy pyrochlores
abstract:
Publication date: 15 January 2027
Source: Computational Materials Science, Volume 277
Author(s): Yuxuan Wang, Huicong Chen, Guoqiang Lan, Jun Song
relevance_reason: Deep-learning interatomic potential development/application for high-entropy pyrochlores, explicitly satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Efficient spin-lattice dynamics and spin thermometry with machine-learned magnetic potentials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32129v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In finite-temperature spin-lattice dynamics, conventional force-only spin thermometers fail for energies nonlinear in each spin, while the standard semi-implicit SIB integrator requires two model evaluations per step. Here we introduce a geometric-probe spin temperature that is exact for arbitrary high-order smooth Hamiltonians using first-order spin forces alone without Hessians, making it naturally suited for nonlinear many-body machine-learning (ML) magnetic potentials. Complementarily, our cached-field integrator (CFI) stays second-order accurate with a single model evaluation per step, about halving the time per step with ML potentials. Extensive benchmarks against Monte Carlo across analytic and ML systems confirm both exact thermometry and accurate thermodynamics.
relevance_reason: Introduces a geometric-probe spin temperature and a cached-field integrator for spin-lattice dynamics with machine-learned magnetic potentials, benchmarked against Monte Carlo on analytic and ML systems, satisfying (a)-(c) as MD/MLIP-driven method development.

title: Structural basis for alpha-actinin inhibition of cofilin binding to actin filaments
abstract: Actin is a conserved cytoskeletal protein essential for morphogenesis, motility, and division. Its versatility arises from filament assembly and regulation by actin binding proteins. Among these, alpha-actinin organizes filaments into bipolar or unipolar networks, whereas cofilin binds preferentially to ADP-actin regions and forms clusters to shorten the half helical pitch (HHP). Here, we investigated the molecular mechanism of how alpha-actinin alters filament and protomer conformations and influences cofilin binding. Using high-speed atomic force microscopy, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, and principal component analysis, we show that alpha-actinin crosslinking stabilizes actin filaments in the canonical helical state, thereby preventing the cofilin-induced helical shortening required for cooperative filament decoration. Stabilization occurs without significant changes in protomer twist and rise and subdomain geometry and maintains a flattened protomer conformation that restricts twisting needed for cofilin binding. Furthermore, myosin II (S1) and cofilin preferentially bind to normal and shortened half-helical structures, respectively. In contrast, the isolated alpha-actinin-1 actin binding domain mutant (ABD-E235K) and wild-type (ABD-WT) induce local transitions from the canonical double-helical filament to the single-helical protofilament, parallel-helical protofilament state (PPS), and nano-ring structures, while only weakly affecting cofilin binding and cluster formation on PPS. Notably, cofilin can bind and form clusters along single protofilaments without inducing helical-pitch shortening. Together, these findings reveal a mechanistically distinct function of full-length alpha-actinin and its isolated ABD and support a stepwise mechanism in which cofilin cooperative binding to canonical double-helical actin filaments requires initial binding to actin regions with shortened HHP, followed by protomer twisting and further helical shortening.
relevance_reason: All-atom molecular dynamics of actin filaments with PCA satisfies (a) explicit atoms, (b) MD, and (c) mechanistic application to a biological system.

title: Metadynamics for vacancy dynamics in crystals
abstract: We propose a metadynamics-based (MetaD) approach to construct the free energy surface (FES) for vacancy dynamics in crystals. In this approach, the vacancy FES can be constructed without explicitly defining a unique vacancy coordinate by introducing a set of parameters that strongly govern the FES, which is enabled by parallel bias MetaD with partitioned families. In addition, the proposed approach is made more efficient and effective by multihill strategy that exploits crystallographic symmetry. We demonstrate the validity and efficacy of the proposed approach through its applications to self-diffusion and impurity diffusion via monovacancies and divacancies in metallic and ionic crystals.
relevance_reason: Metadynamics free-energy-surface construction for vacancy migration in crystals satisfies (a) explicit atomic crystals, (b) enhanced sampling/free-energy method, and (c) method advance validated on self- and impurity diffusion.

title: First-principles phase diagram of monolayer CrS$_2$ polymorphs under biaxial strain and its sensitivity to the Hubbard U parameter
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32265v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: In correlated two-dimensional magnets the balance between competing electronic and magnetic phases is often set by the strength of the on-site Coulomb interaction, so that the predicted ground state can hinge on a parameter that is not uniquely defined. Monolayer CrS$_2$ lies squarely in this regime, hosting several energetically close polymorphs whose character ranges from non-magnetic semiconducting to magnetically ordered metallic. We therefore investigate, using DFT$+U$ within the generalized gradient approximation, the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the 1H, 1T, 1T$'$, and 1T$''$ polymorphs of monolayer CrS$_2$ under varying Hubbard interactions ($U=0$--$8$~eV) and biaxial strain ($-10\%$ to $+10\%$). The 1T-derived structures remain metallic and magnetic throughout, with $U$ acting mainly as a spectral renormalization. The 1H phase behaves differently, passing from a non-magnetic semiconductor through an antiferromagnetic semiconducting regime before metallizing, so that the gap closes as $U$ increases while the local Cr moment grows monotonically. Biaxial tensile strain at fixed $U$ induces a similar sequence of transitions. Along both tuning pathways, the two inequivalent nearest-neighbor Cr--Cr exchange channels progressively separate and cross, with the parallel-spin channel becoming dominant, accompanied by a breathing-type bond disproportionation. Independent calculations with a localized-orbital implementation reproduce the overall evolution but yield shifted critical values of $U$ and of strain, demonstrating the robustness of the phase diagram while highlighting the implementation dependence of the transition thresholds.
relevance_reason: DFT+U calculations with structural relaxation and phase-diagram construction on explicit monolayer CrS2 polymorphs satisfy (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT, and (c) method-parameter study (U, strain) of magnetic/electronic phases.

title: Systematic and accurate anharmonic formation free energies of metastable defects via a constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force framework
abstract:
arXiv:2608.20902v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Computing the formation free energies of metastable defects at finite temperature remains challenging due to anharmonicity, the multiplicity of basins and the frequent occurrence of migration events. Using the previously introduced constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force method (BABFc), we establish a practical thermodynamic integration framework for computing restricted anharmonic formation free energies associated with individual metastable defect basins. We demonstrate that BABFc can be exploited as a robust, systematic and numerically efficient tool for addressing a long standing bottleneck in atomistic materials science: the finite temperature thermodynamic characterization of metastable defects in complex, highly anharmonic energy landscapes. The proposed workflow requires only a reference local minimum and a confinement strategy and does not rely on defect specific collective variables. It therefore provides a general route to assign well-defined free energies to individual metastable basins, even when these basins are separated by low barriers and embedded in a dense landscape of competing configurations. In this setting, BABFc enables stable, bias corrected free energy estimates with statistical accuracies at the meV/atom level and a very low failure rate, including for systems containing approximately one thousand atoms. We demonstrate this capability through thousands of independent free energy calculations covering hundreds of four-interstitial and four-vacancy configurations in bcc $\alpha$-Fe over a broad temperature range, using both a traditional empirical potential and a data driven force field.
relevance_reason: Establishes a constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force / thermodynamic integration framework for anharmonic formation free energies of metastable defects with meV/atom accuracy in systems of ~1000 atoms; explicit atoms (a), free-energy/enhanced-sampling methodology (b), and an applied atomistic materials problem (c) are all satisfied.

title: Stability and optoelectronic properties of oligothiophene molecules confined in boron-nitride nanotubes: A many-body theoretical approach
abstract:
Author(s): Xavier Blase, Mauricio Rodriguez-Mayorga, and Ivan Duchemin
We investigate the structural and optoelectronic properties of oligothiophene (nT) molecules encapsulated in boron-nitride (BN) nanotubes using density functional theory, many-body $GW$ and Bethe-Salpeter equation approaches. We show that the binding energy is maximized for tube diameters of approxi…

relevance_reason: It applies DFT, GW, and Bethe-Salpeter equation calculations to explicit oligothiophene/BN-nanotube atomistic structures, satisfying (a), (b), and (c).

title: Current-Dependent Meta-GGA and Local Hybrid Functionals for Relativistic NMR Shifts
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31432v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: NMR chemical shifts are key for the characterization of novel compounds. Especially for molecules with heavy elements, the experimental data is often corroborated with computational studies in density functional theory (DFT). However, modern meta-generalized gradient approximations (meta-GGAs) and local hybrid functionals are not widely supported in relativistic calculations with quantum chemistry program suites. So far, their current-dependent generalization in the spirit of Dobson, Becke, and Tao was not presented at all. This generalization ensures gauge invariance and does not introduce artifacts--unlike the more popular field-dependent generalization of the kinetic-energy density. In non-relativistic and scalar-relativistic calculations, the first was shown to be superior but the current density only arises due to the magnetic field perturbation. In contrast, spin--orbit coupling also induces current densities in the preceding ground-state calculation and the DFT framework needs to be generalized to a current density functional theory (CDFT) for consistency with the current-dependent response equations. Herein, we present the two-component relativistic generalization of the current-dependent kinetic-energy density of a Kramers-restricted Kohn--Sham reference for meta-GGAs and local hybrid functionals in NMR calculations. The extension is invariant under a position-dependent phase and a position-dependent spin rotation of the spinors, or a local U(1)$\times$SU(2) transformation. Relativistic effects are considered with exact two-component theory using a superposition of atomic potentials to include the two-electron picture-change correction (SAP-X2C).
relevance_reason: DFT functional development for relativistic NMR shifts using current-dependent meta-GGA/local hybrids on explicit molecular atoms satisfies (a), and the DFT method advance satisfies (b)-(c).

title: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22284v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory (DFT) to include a temperature dimension. The formalism unifies established hybrid functionals with information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation DFT, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. It further gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set of different organic molecules. The results clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.
relevance_reason: DFT hybrid-functional development with a temperature dimension benchmarked on organic molecules satisfies (a)-(c) via explicit atoms and DFT method advance.

title: Interfragment Population Suppression in Density Functional Theory

title: Efficient all-electron Bethe-Salpeter implementation using crystal symmetries
abstract:
Author(s): Jörn Stöhler, Stefan Blügel, and Christoph Friedrich
The authors describe here an all-electron implementation of the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) within the full-potential linearized augmented-plane-wave (FLAPW) method, using a mixed basis for the Coulomb interaction potentials and an analytical treatment of the Coulomb divergence. Group theory is exploited to block-diagonalize the two-particle Hamiltonian, substantially reducing the computational cost. The parallelized code supports spin-orbit coupling and distributed memory. Calculated optical spectra and exciton binding energies for Si, LiF, and MoS2 agree well with available theoretical and experimental results.
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285127] Published Tue Nov 24, 2026
relevance_reason: It develops an all-electron FLAPW Bethe-Salpeter equation implementation for optical spectra of explicit crystals; it satisfies (a) via atomistic crystal representations, (b) via DFT/electronic-structure method development, and (c) by advancing a first-principles atomistic method.

title: Controlling vertical and lateral growth of copper and ruthenium on tungsten dichalcogenide monolayers for interconnects and metal contacts
abstract: Tungsten-based transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers (TMDs) show significant promise in applications including catalysis, semiconductors, and sensors. A key requirement is interfacing the TMDs with metals. Controlling the morphology of the interfaced metal is critical for performance. Atomic level simulations can be used to predict how metals interact and grow on TMDs. First principles studies of metal-TMDs have focused on single metal adatom interactions, or pristine metal–monolayer interfaces. Consequently, there persists a gap in predicting metal growth on TMDs, limiting optimization of TMD-metal interfaces for new technologies. We present a density functional theory study of Cu and Ru deposit adsorption and dynamics on WS2 and WSe2 monolayers. By characterizing the behavior of metal deposits that display a variety of potential morphologies with an ensemble of analytical shape descriptors derived from the gyration tensor, we develop a quantitative description of the morphology and dynamics of deposited metals on TMDs. This approach allows direct comparison of metal deposit morphologies on different substrates. On both TMDs, Cu prefers to form compact, vertically growing clusters, suitable for catalysis and sensing, while Ru prefers lateral growth suitable for interconnects and contacts in next-generation semiconductors. Dynamics simulations show that temperature promotes further growth in the favored direction, providing a route for interface optimization after initial deposition.
relevance_reason: DFT study of Cu and Ru deposit adsorption, morphology, and dynamics on WS2/WSe2 monolayers satisfies (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT/geometry optimization and dynamics, and (c) applies them to metal-on-TMD growth.

title: Membrane thickness strain from protein inclusions: A multiscale simulation and x-ray scattering study of proteoliposomes
abstract: Integral membrane proteins remodel the surrounding lipid bilayer, but quantifying the resulting deformations and linking them to protein density in the membrane has remained challenging. Here, we introduce an integrative methodology that combines all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with multiscale small-angle x-ray scattering (SAXS) analysis to connect membrane thickness strain to the protein/lipid ratio in proteoliposomes. Using outer membrane phospholipase A (OmpLA) reconstituted into lipid bilayers with either larger or smaller hydrophobic thickness, we systematically probe the effects of positive and negative hydrophobic mismatch. MD simulations demonstrate that OmpLA causes anisotropic, oscillatory thickness deformations extending up to eight times the radius of the first lipid shell surrounding the protein, yet the net change in average membrane thickness remains below 1%. Through our multiscale SAXS analysis, we quantitatively extract structural parameters, ranging from proteoliposome size to internal membrane architecture, using constrained Bayesian inference, with priors derived from MD findings. Specifically, we determine the average membrane thickness strain, yielding values consistent with MD simulations, and the protein/lipid molar ratio. In thinner bilayers, substantial protein loss limits the analysis, highlighting the role of bilayer stability in sample preparation. Moreover, the predominance of OmpLA monomers in the thicker membranes is consistent with weak, membrane-mediated repulsive interactions between protein inclusions. Collectively, this integrative approach establishes a framework for quantifying protein–lipid interactions across molecular and mesoscale dimensions.
relevance_reason: All-atom MD of OmpLA in lipid bilayers combined with SAXS/Bayesian inference satisfies (a) explicit atoms, (b) classical MD, and (c) quantification of membrane thickness strain.

title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31672v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting is considered as one of the most promising approaches for the green hydrogen production. But the rapid recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs severely inhibits its photocatalytic efficiency. Construction of van der Waals heterostructures is a good way to suppress this recombination. However, in staggered band heterostructures, the charge transfer could occur either through the type-II or the direct Z-scheme mechanism. Therefore it is very important to identify which mechanism is dominant. In the present work, we systematically study the GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure using first-principles density functional theory (DFT). The system exhibits good thermodynamic, dynamic and thermal stability and an indirect band gap of 1.38 eV which greatly enhances the visible-light absorption. We find that the direct Z-scheme mechanism is the dominant interfacial charge transfer by analysing band alignment and Gibbs free energy pathways. The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) can be driven spontaneously in the pH range $4 \le \text{pH} \le 14$ under light irradiation for both type-II and Z-scheme pathways but the energy barrier is much lower for the Z-scheme mechanism. Moreover, the type-II mechanism is not suitable for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), but the Z-scheme mechanism can promote HER well in the entire pH range ($0 \le \text{pH} \le 14$). Remarkably, the strain-free (pristine) condition exhibits a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 41.40\%, well above the 10\% threshold for commercial viability. The STH efficiency is further enhanced to 60.68\% under a tensile strain of +6\%. To summarise, the Z-scheme strain-tunable GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure is a promising and efficient photocatalyst for overall water splitting.
relevance_reason: First-principles DFT calculations on explicit GeC/ReS2 heterostructure atomic models satisfy (a)-(b), and the application to photocatalytic water splitting satisfies (c).

title: Mixing and Preserving Properties of Non-van der Waals 2D Materials in Sandwich-like Heterostructures
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32723v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Heterostructure interfaces created by stacking two-dimensional (2D) materials outline an appealing route towards achieving advanced electronic and magnetic functionalities at the nanoscale. Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) sandwich-like heterostructures (HSs) are build out of non-vdW 2D materials derived from non-layered crystals and establish a new frontier enabling strong interfacial coupling. Employing ab initio density functional theory (DFT), we investigate two classes of such trilayer HSs: purely non-vdW assemblies and hybrid vdW/non-vdW/vdW stacks. We show that non-vdW sandwiches undergo pronounced geometric reconstruction forming chemically bonded interfaces with large absolute binding energies up to an order of magnitude larger than those of conventional vdW HSs. These strong interactions drive extensive electronic hybridization, band gap renormalization, and tunable interlayer magnetic coupling. In contrast, vdW encapsulation largely protects the intrinsic atomic and electronic structure of the non-vdW sheet from the environment , while enabling charge transfer doping of the vdW layers. Our results thus establish sandwich HSs a versatile interface design platform, spanning interaction regimes from weakly perturbed encapsulation to strongly interacting chemically bonded systems with emergent electronic and magnetic behavior.
relevance_reason: Ab initio DFT calculations (relaxation, binding energies, band structure, magnetic coupling) on explicit atom trilayer heterostructures; (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT geometry optimization/energetics, (c) applied to understand interfacial electronic/magnetic properties are all satisfied.

title: Is there a density-gradient expansion for the electronic exchange energy?
abstract: An old but recurring question in ground-state density functional theory, relevant to the construction of density functional approximations, is the existence of a second-order gradient expansion for the exchange energy that is exact for densities that vary slowly over space. Here, we will argue that there is such an expansion, with a gradient coefficient 10/7 of Sham’s, as suggested by theoretical/mathematical derivations and by numerical calculations on model slowly varying metallic densities, although some standard derivations do not quite capture the correct gradient coefficient. We also discuss long-range anomalies in the gradient expansions for the exchange and correlation holes around an electron. It is plausible that, as suggested earlier and recently, standard derivations are still correct for the coefficient of the second-order gradient expansion for exchange and correlation together, in which case the correct gradient coefficient for correlation is Cc=Cxc−Cx. We propose possible numerical evaluations of Cxc and Cx that are free from long-range anomalies, and discuss implications for density functional approximations. Axel Becke’s 1988 generalized gradient approximation (the B88 GGA) for the exchange energy brought density functional theory into chemistry, with a gradient coefficient for exchange that is optimal at the GGA level for atoms and molecules but too large for solids. Meta-GGAs seem to work as well for molecules as for solids, but may not be perfected yet. The article concludes with a few memories that the first author has of discussions with Axel Becke.
relevance_reason: Density-functional-theory method development on the gradient expansion of the exchange energy satisfies (b) DFT functional development and (c); it is a DFT-approximation advance even without a specific dynamics application.

title: Energy-Guided Generative Modeling for Low-Energy Molecular Structure Discovery
abstract:
arXiv:2512.22597v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Exploring molecular energy landscapes and identifying ground-state conformations are central challenges in computational chemistry. However, generating diverse low-energy conformers from molecular graphs remains expensive with traditional physics-based pipelines. Existing learning-based approaches remain fragmented: generative models capture conformational diversity but often lack reliable energy calibration, whereas deterministic predictors focus on a single structure and fail to represent ensemble variability. Here we introduce EnFlow, to our knowledge, the first energy-guided generative framework that couples flow-based conformer generation with explicit energy landscape modeling for joint conformational ensemble generation and ground-state identification. By integrating generative dynamics with a learned energy model, EnFlow guides sampling toward low-energy regions of the conformational landscape, improving structural fidelity under extremely few sampling steps while enabling energy-based ranking of generated conformations. Experiments on GEOM-QM9 and GEOM-Drugs show that EnFlow achieves strong performance in conformer generation and ground-state identification while requiring only 1-2 ordinary differential equation (ODE) sampling steps. Single-point GFN2-xTB evaluations further show that the learned energy scores preserve physically meaningful energetic rankings of generated conformations. These results support explicit energy landscape modeling as an effective strategy for low-energy molecular structure discovery through joint modeling of conformational ensembles and their associated energies.
relevance_reason: A flow-based generative model produces 3D conformers and ranks them with an energy model validated by GFN2-xTB single points, satisfying (a)-(c) via explicit atomic configurations and energetic validation.

title: Thermodynamics of complex crystals from a generalized mean-field bond model
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32609v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We extend our previously introduced mean-field bond model from unary fcc lattices to crystals with multiple chemical species and sublattices, accurately predicting finite-temperature thermodynamics without statistical sampling. Our generalization reformulates the model in terms of the Wyckoff positions of the crystal, representing each by one atom, and solving for the bond density of the reference bond of each of its neighbor shells. Bond-bond correlation functions are built from the zero-temperature force constants, allowing the deviation of every bond in the crystal to be expressed through linear functions of the reference bond of a shell. Thermodynamic self-consistency is enforced by requiring a single virial temperature for the whole crystal, and compatibility of average bond lengths with crystal volume. Model predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations of unary, binary, and ternary crystals using Morse-type bonding potentials, parametrized for each shell from the force constants of empirical interatomic potentials at several isotropic strains. In each case, the predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with the simulations to within their statistical uncertainty. We discuss strategies for combining the model with bonding potentials parametrized from first principles and foundation models to predict the finite-temperature thermodynamics of complex crystals at ab initio accuracy without statistical sampling.
relevance_reason: Classical molecular dynamics with Morse-type bonding potentials on explicit crystals validates a thermodynamic mean-field bond model, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33060v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Native vacancy populations in transition-metal nitride coatings reflect vacancy formation, association, and depth-dependent stability. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compare these effects in rocksalt TiN and CrN in bulk and at (001) surfaces, within phase-stability-constrained chemical potential ranges. In TiN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ is favoured under N-poor and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ under N-rich conditions; in CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ remains preferred throughout its stability range. Association energies are referenced to corresponding isolated vacancies where positive values mean association lowers the energy and negative values favour separation. Mean bulk association energies for mixed metal-nitrogen pairs are $+0.132$ eV in TiN and $+1.053$ eV in CrN. At (001) surfaces, $V_\mathrm{N}$ in TiN prefers the surface and $V_\mathrm{Ti}$ the first subsurface layer. In CrN, $V_\mathrm{N}$ has similar formation energies at the surface and first subsurface layer, with a slight preference for the latter; $V_\mathrm{Cr}$ slightly prefers the second subsurface layer. Surface cluster energies are referenced to separated vacancies at their preferred depths. The compact $2V_\mathrm{Ti}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ cluster in TiN has favourable association in bulk ($+0.217$ eV per vacancy) but unfavourable association at the surface ($-0.346$ eV per vacancy). By contrast, $2V_\mathrm{Cr}+2V_\mathrm{N}$ in CrN remains stabilised, with its association energy decreasing from $+1.188$ to $+0.431$ eV per vacancy. CrN's stronger association occurs without larger structural distortions and is accompanied by distinct Cr-centred magnetic responses.
relevance_reason: DFT supercell total-energy calculations of vacancy formation, association, and surface clustering in TiN and CrN with explicit atoms; (a) explicit atoms in periodic cells, (b) DFT energetics/geometry optimization, (c) applied to defect physics, all satisfied, though no dynamics.

title: Systematic Magnetic Structure Generation Based on Oriented Spin Space Groups: Formulation, Applications, and High-Throughput First-Principles Calculations
abstract:
arXiv:2601.15735v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We propose a framework for generating magnetic structures, inspired by the concept of oriented spin space groups (SSGs): Magnetic structures are first generated as totally symmetric representations of an SSG and are then rotated such that they belong to the maximal magnetic space group of the SSG, which we term spin-symmetry-adapted (SSA) structures and oriented SSA structures, respectively. This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. In the MAGNDATA database, 77% of the reported structures are reproducible at the SSG level, among which 82% are fully reproduced within the oriented SSG scheme, regardless of their spin-only group types or propagation vectors. With the $k$ index fixed to its experimental value, about nine structures are generated per material on average. We perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. The characteristic energy scale among oriented SSA structures is only approximately 0.29 meV per magnetic atom, about 300 times smaller than that of distinct SSA structures. These results demonstrate that oriented SSG-based enumeration, combined with the two-step calculations for SSA and oriented SSA structures, provides an efficient and robust route for large-scale magnetic-structure prediction.
relevance_reason: Symmetry-based magnetic structure enumeration validated by spin-polarized DFT (with SOC) energy calculations for 283 materials on explicit atomic structures satisfies (a)-(c).

title: ZStar: A unified toolkit for polarization, Born effective charges, dielectric and piezoelectric responses, and infrared and Raman spectra
abstract:
arXiv:2609.16802v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Polarization and the response to atomic displacements determine the dielectric, piezoelectric, and vibrational spectroscopy of materials, yet these quantities are usually obtained through separate workflows within ABACUS. Here, we present ZStar, an open-source Python toolkit that unifies these calculations. Using ABACUS and PYATB, ZStar derives Born effective charges (BECs) and zone-center force constants from one symmetry-adapted displacement set, and reuses the displaced electronic matrices for Raman spectra. Berry phases in periodic directions combined with charge-density dipoles in nonperiodic directions extend the method from bulk crystals (3D) to 2D and 1D materials and molecules (0D). These BECs and phonon modes give infrared intensities and the lattice contribution to the dielectric response. From finite strains, ZStar further obtains clamped-ion and relaxed-ion piezoelectric coefficients. This unified workflow reduces the computational cost by up to 4.2$\times$ for BECs and zone-center phonons and 8.4$\times$ for combined infrared and Raman calculations. ZStar also supports machine-learned models by generating training data and post-processing prediction results into physical properties.
relevance_reason: ZStar is a DFT-based toolkit (ABACUS/PYATB) computing Born effective charges, force constants, phonons, and piezoelectric/dielectric responses from symmetry-adapted atomic displacements, satisfying (a)-(c) as electronic-structure method/tool development with MLIP training-data support.
